A sunburst chart is a multi-level donut for **hierarchical composition**: each ring is one level of the hierarchy, angular width is proportional to a value (counts, cost), and segments nest radially from root to leaves \[1\]. Compared with a treemap it emphasizes the *levels* of the hierarchy; compared with stacked pies it keeps every level quantitative and interactive (hover to inspect, click to zoom into a subtree). In clinical data it shines for cohorts that decompose naturally — cancer type → treatment line → response, or department → diagnosis group → procedure.

This tutorial builds sunbursts with `plotly` \[2\] using the `ids`/`labels`/`parents`/`values` node table. Because the figure is an interactive HTML widget, the rendered page supports hover tooltips and click-to-zoom.

This tutorial covers two workflows:

1. A basic three-level cohort sunburst;
2. A color-coded variant with per-branch colors and hover text.

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming language: R

-   Dependent packages: `plotly`; `dplyr`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
# Load packages
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

We simulate an oncology cohort of 270 patients across three cancer types, two treatment lines, and three response categories (PR = partial response, SD = stable disease, PD = progressive disease). The node table needs exactly four columns: `id` (unique path), `label`, `parent` (empty for roots), and `value` (the leaf count; with `branchvalues = "total"` every parent's value must equal the sum of its children).

```{r load data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(251)

coh <- data.frame(
  cancer = rep(c("Breast", "Lung (NSCLC)", "Colorectal"), each = 90),
  line   = rep(c("1st line", "2nd line+"), each = 45, times = 3),
  response = c(rep(c("PR", "SD", "PD"), times = c(28, 12, 5)),
               rep(c("PR", "SD", "PD"), times = c(15, 18, 12)),
               rep(c("PR", "SD", "PD"), times = c(30, 10, 5)),
               rep(c("PR", "SD", "PD"), times = c(10, 20, 15)),
               rep(c("PR", "SD", "PD"), times = c(22, 15, 8)),
               rep(c("PR", "SD", "PD"), times = c(8, 22, 15)))
)
cnt <- coh |> count(cancer, line, response, name = "n")

nodes <- bind_rows(
  # roots: one per cancer type
  data.frame(id = unique(cnt$cancer), label = unique(cnt$cancer), parent = "",
             value = sapply(unique(cnt$cancer), function(x) sum(cnt$n[cnt$cancer == x]))),
  # level 2: treatment lines
  cnt |>
    distinct(cancer, line) |>
    mutate(id = paste(cancer, line), label = line, parent = cancer,
           value = sapply(paste(cancer, line), function(x) sum(cnt$n[paste(cnt$cancer, cnt$line) == x]))) |>
    select(id, label, parent, value),
  # level 3: responses
  cnt |>
    mutate(id = paste(cancer, line, response), label = response,
           parent = paste(cancer, line), value = n) |>
    select(id, label, parent, value)
)

# parent values must equal the sum of their children (branchvalues = "total")
stopifnot(all(sapply(unique(nodes$parent[nodes$parent != ""]),
                     function(p) sum(nodes$value[nodes$parent == p]) ==
                       nodes$value[nodes$id == p])))
```

## Visualization

### 1. Basic Cohort Sunburst

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1Sunburst
#| fig-cap: "Three-level sunburst of the oncology cohort: inner ring = cancer type, middle = treatment line, outer = response. Hover shows counts; click a segment to zoom into its subtree."
#| out.width: "80%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false

fig1 <- plot_ly(
  type = "sunburst",
  ids = nodes$id, labels = nodes$label,
  parents = nodes$parent, values = nodes$value,
  branchvalues = "total",
  hovertemplate = "%{id}<br>n = %{value}<extra></extra>"
) |>
  layout(title = "Oncology cohort: type → line → response")
fig1
```

### 2. Color-Coded Sunburst

```{r}
#| label: fig-2.1SunburstColored
#| fig-cap: "The same hierarchy with per-branch colors inherited down the tree; response segments carry hover text with the response rate within their parent branch."
#| out.width: "80%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false

cols <- setNames(c("#4E79A7", "#F28E2B", "#E15759"), unique(cnt$cancer))

resp_rate <- cnt |>
  group_by(cancer, line) |>
  mutate(rate = scales::percent(n / sum(n), accuracy = 1)) |>
  ungroup()
lbls <- resp_rate |>
  mutate(id = paste(cancer, line, response),
         label = paste0(response, " · ", rate))

fig2 <- plot_ly(
  type = "sunburst",
  ids = nodes$id, labels = lbls$label[match(nodes$id, lbls$id)],
  parents = nodes$parent, values = nodes$value,
  branchvalues = "total",
  marker = list(colors = ifelse(nodes$parent == "", "#8C8C8C",
                                cols[substr(nodes$parent, 1, nchar(nodes$parent))])),
  textinfo = "label",
  insidetextorientation = "radial",
  hovertemplate = "%{id}<br>n = %{value}<extra></extra>"
) |>
  layout(title = "Response rates within each treatment line")
fig2
```

::: callout-tip
## Practice tips

-   With `branchvalues = "total"`, parent `value`s must equal the sum of their children — validate the node table programmatically (as in Data Preparation) or plotly draws overlapping wedges. Alternatively use `branchvalues = "remainder"` and give parents only their own value.
-   Keep `id`s unique full paths (`paste(parent, child)`) — duplicated ids silently merge subtrees.
-   Sunbursts read badly beyond ~3 levels and ~30 leaves; collapse rare categories into an "Other" segment first.
-   Static export for print figures needs a screenshot of the widget — the `webshot2` package or a browser screenshot; hover interactivity is the web version's advantage.
:::

## Application

Sunbursts are used for cohort composition (registry papers), cost decomposition (diagnosis → procedure), and taxonomic abundance (metagenomics: phylum → genus → species). The panel below mirrors a typical publication layout: (A) the full hierarchy and (B) the response-rate variant.
